issues: No integrity problems found. The diff changes one line: WINDOW_PATTERN goes from "SSSL" to "SSL", so more layers use full-context attention. It does not touch the metric, the data, the seed lines or the evaluation call.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. "SSL" is a valid pattern made of the same S/L characters, so the run measures what it claims to.
The numbers support the reject decision. The candidate scored 1.0999 against the incumbent's 1.0952, so it is 0.0047 worse (lower is better). The negative z has the right sign.

I can't recompute z exactly because the noise estimate (sigma) is not given. Assuming z = diff / sigma, z = -0.606 implies sigma of about 0.0078. There is only one run on each side, so the evidence is weak, but nothing points towards a gain.
Extra full-attention layers cost more compute per step, so fewer steps fit in the fixed 300 s. That makes the worse result plausible.
